'''Brooke Olivia van Velden'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20201125_039660000/event|title = Speech – New Zealand Parliament}}</ref> (born 15 October 1992)<ref>{{Cite web|last=van Velden|first=Brooke|date=14 October 2020|title=Thank you to the ACT team for the birthday surprise and well wishes 💛 First one as an MP and one to remember!|url=https://www.facebook.com/login/?next=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2FbrookeACT%2Fposts%2F3085606125011245|url-status=live|access-date=17 October 2021|website=Facebook|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211017083627/https://www.facebook.com/login/?next=https://www.facebook.com/brookeACT/posts/3085606125011245 |archive-date=17 October 2021 }}</ref><ref name="Hansard 10 Feb">{{cite web|url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20210210_052380000/van-velden-brooke-mallard-trevor|title=van Velden, Brooke; Mallard, Trevor|date=10 February 2021|publisher=New Zealand Parliament}}</ref> is a New Zealand politician who served as the deputy leader of [[ACT New Zealand]] from June 2020 to June 2026.<ref>{{Cite news |date= 17 October 2020 |title=ACT deputy leader Brooke van Velden a novice MP but has plenty of political experience |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/300135520/act-deputy-leader-brooke-van-velden-a-novice-mp-but-has-plenty-of-political-experience |access-date=18 October 2020 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] }}</ref><ref name="Website-1" /> She has been a [[member of Parliament]] (MP) since the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 general election]], first as a [[list MP]]<ref name="40 new MPs">{{Cite news |via=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |title=Election 2020: The 40 diverse new MPs entering Parliament |url= https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/news/vote-2020/election-2020-the-forty-newcomers-entering-parliament/ |date=18 October 2020 |access-date=16 November 2020 |work=[[Newstalk ZB]] |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201022040442/https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/news/vote-2020/election-2020-the-forty-newcomers-entering-parliament/ |archive-date=22 October 2020}}</ref> and, since {{NZ election link year|2023}}, the MP for [[Tāmaki (New Zealand electorate)|Tāmaki]]. Van Velden currently serves in the [[Sixth National Government of New Zealand|National-led government]] as the 38th [[Minister of Internal Affairs (New Zealand)|minister of internal affairs]] and 6th [[Minister for Workplace Relations and Safety|minister for workplace relations and safety]]. She is the second youngest cabinet minister in New Zealand history, being just eight days older than [[Phil Goff]] was when he became Minister of Housing after the 1984 election.

Van Velden has announced she will retire from politics at the [[2026 New Zealand general election|2026 general election]].<ref name="z239">{{cite web |date=23 March 2026 |title=Act deputy Van Velden to step down |url=https://newsroom.co.nz/2026/03/24/van-velden-to-step-down/ |access-date=23 March 2026 |website=Newsroom}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Van Velden was born in Auckland in 1992.<ref name="Hansard 10 Feb"/> She attended [[St Cuthbert's College, Auckland|St Cuthbert's College]] in Auckland, where she joined the school choir in Year 12. She says this sparked her interest in public speaking. She later joined the Welsh Choir.<ref name="Now to Love 2023">{{cite news |last1=Milford |first1=Catherine |title=MP Brooke van Velden's accidental foray into politics |url=https://www.nowtolove.co.nz/news/latest-news/brooke-van-velden-politics-47700 |access-date=5 February 2024 |work=Now to Love |publisher=[[Are Media]] |date=21 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240117012328/https://www.nowtolove.co.nz/news/latest-news/brooke-van-velden-politics-47700 |archive-date=17 January 2024}}</ref>

Van Velden studied economics and international trade at the [[University of Auckland]], graduating with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] and [[Bachelor of Commerce]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.auckland.ac.nz/en/for/current-students/cs-academic-information/cs-graduation-information/cs-graduation-search-and-confirmation/cs-graduation-search-results.html |title=Graduation search results |publisher=[[University of Auckland]] |accessdate=9 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="Now to Love 2023" /> She worked for lobbying firm Exceltium.<ref name="stuffannounce">{{cite news |last1=Cooke |first1=Henry |title=ACT reveals new list, elects 27-year-old staffer deputy leader and puts gun lobbyist at number three |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/300044090/act-reveals-new-list-elects-27yearold-staffer-deputy-leader-and-puts-gun-lobbyist-at-number-three |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |access-date=28 June 2020 |date=28 June 2020}}</ref>

==Early political career==
=== Political staffer and lobbyist ===
{{See also|End of Life Choice Act 2019}}
Before becoming a Member of Parliament, van Velden worked as a staffer for ACT leader [[David Seymour (New Zealand politician)|David Seymour]]. Her sole task in this role was to get Seymour's [[End of Life Choice Act 2019|End of Life Choice Bill]] passed. She spent two years lobbying Members of Parliament to support it and helped draft the legislation.<ref name="Now to Love 2023" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Manch|first=Thomas|date=16 November 2019|title=Formidable Brooke van Velden: The End of Life Choice bill lobbyist you've probably never heard of|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/health/euthanasia-debate/117370430/formidable-brooke-van-velden-the-end-of-life-choice-bill-lobbyist-youve-probably-never-heard-of|access-date=23 October 2020|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}}</ref>  Van Velden said that she "made herself useful" to MPs who wanted to know more about the bill, and also approached politicians in the tunnel between the [[Beehive (New Zealand)|Beehive]] and the Bowen Street building to discuss the bill. She said that she has been called a "snake" and a "spy", and that once several MPs had shouted abuse at her.<ref name=":0" />

The Bill passed and became an Act of Parliament in 2019,<ref name="3rd">{{cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/beehive-live/117384206/mps-vote-on-final-reading-of-end-of-life-choice-bill|title=MPs vote in favour of End of Life Choice Bill at final reading|work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]|author=Henry Cooke|date=13 November 2019|access-date=13 November 2019}}</ref> but with concessions. The bill faced opposition from members of the Justice Select Committee in 2018. Seymour and van Velden developed a "sponsor's report" for the bill, giving their own recommendations before the committee, including limiting assisted death only to those who were terminally ill. This compromise restricted choice but improved support. The Act also states that it only comes into effect if supported by a referendum.<ref name=":0" /> This referendum was held on 17 October and it passed with 65.1% support.<ref>{{Cite web|date=6 November 2020|title='No' vote for cannabis legalisation shrinks to 50.7 percent after final votes|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/430007/no-vote-for-cannabis-legalisation-shrinks-to-50-point-7-percent-after-final-votes|access-date=6 November 2020|website=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}}</ref>

===2017 election candidacy===
Van Velden first ran for Parliament at the [[2017 New Zealand general election|2017 general election]]. She contested the {{NZ electorate link|Auckland Central}} electorate<ref name="RNZ2017">{{cite news |title=First time candidate: Brooke van Velden |url= https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/sunday/audio/201846285/first-time-candidate-brooke-van-velden |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |access-date=28 June 2020 |date=4 June 2017}}</ref> and was placed third on ACT's party list,<ref name="stuffannounce" /> but was not elected.<ref>{{cite web |title=Official Count Results – Auckland Central (2017) |url= http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2017/electorate-details-01.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |date=7 October 2017 |access-date=7 November 2020}}</ref>

[[File:Brooke van Velden 2023 half shot.jpg|150px|left|thumb|Brooke van Velden during the formation of the Sixth National Government in November 2023.]]
Van Velden was selected as ACT's deputy leader in June 2020, at the age of 27, and was placed second on its party list for the 2020 general election. At the announcement of her role, leader David Seymour described her as the "future of the party".<ref name="stuffannounce" /> She ran for the electorate of {{NZ electorate link|Wellington Central}}.<ref name="stuffannounce" /> She did not win the electorate, placing fifth with 865 votes, but ACT, with 7.6% of the preliminary party vote, was entitled to ten MPs including van Velden.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wellington Central – Official Result |url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-60.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=6 November 2020 }}</ref><ref name="results2020">{{cite web |date=6 November 2020 |title=2020 General Election and Referendums – Official Result |url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/ |access-date=6 November 2020 |website=Electoral Commission}}</ref> As Seymour was previously the party's only representative in Parliament, van Velden became one of nine new ACT Party MPs in the [[53rd New Zealand Parliament|53rd Parliament]].<ref name="40 new MPs" /><!-- this source lists the 40 new members according to the preliminary results --><ref><!-- this reference confirms that it's now 42 new members; new ACT MPs are not affected -->{{cite news |last1=Lynch |first1=Jenna |title=NZ Election 2020: Judith Collins will 'definitely not' stand down as leader despite National's crushing defeat |url= https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/11/nz-election-2020-judith-collins-will-definitely-not-stand-down-as-leader-despite-national-s-crushing-defeat.html |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201106055203/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/11/nz-election-2020-judith-collins-will-definitely-not-stand-down-as-leader-despite-national-s-crushing-defeat.html |url-status= dead |archive-date= 6 November 2020 |access-date=8 November 2020 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=6 November 2020}}</ref> In addition to being deputy leader, she is the ACT party whip and spokesperson for Health, Housing, Foreign Affairs, and Trade.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brooke van Velden |url=https://www.act.org.nz/brooke_van_velden |publisher=[[ACT New Zealand]] |access-date=22 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Brooke van Velden |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/members-of-parliament/van-velden-brooke/ |access-date=6 November 2020 |publisher=[[New Zealand Parliament]]}}</ref>

On 19 May 2021, van Velden on behalf of her party opposed [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|Green Party]] MP [[Golriz Ghahraman]]'s motion calling for Members of Parliament to recognise the rights of Palestinians to [[self-determination]] and statehood while reaffirming the Act Party's support for a [[two-state solution]] to the [[Israel-Palestine conflict]]. Van Velden justified ACT's opposition on the basis of another Green MP [[Ricardo Menéndez March]]'s tweet that said "From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free!" In response, Ghahraman contended that March was defending the rights of both Arabs and Jews to having equal rights in their homeland.<ref>{{cite news |title= Green Party motion to call for recognition of Palestine's right to self-determination |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/442887/green-party-motion-to-call-for-recognition-of-palestine-s-right-to-self-determination |access-date=21 May 2021 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=19 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520003402/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/442887/green-party-motion-to-call-for-recognition-of-palestine-s-right-to-self-determination |archive-date=20 May 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Manch |first1=Thomas |title=Green Party's motion to declare Palestine a state fails in Parliament |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/125175638/green-partys-motion-to-declare-palestine-a-state-fails-in-parliament |access-date=21 May 2021 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=19 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520053549/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/125175638/green-partys-motion-to-declare-palestine-a-state-fails-in-parliament |archive-date=20 May 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Member's bill===
Van Velden's [[Private member's bill|member's bill]], the Housing Infrastructure (GST-sharing) Bill, was selected for first reading in October 2022. If passed, it would require the Government to share half of the GST revenue of a new house with the [[Territorial authorities of New Zealand|territorial authority]] responsible for the district the house is built in.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ACT deputy calls for change to house infrastructure funding |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2022/10/16/act-deputy-calls-for-change-to-house-infrastructure-funding/ |date=26 October 2022 |access-date=12 December 2022 |work=[[1News]] |publisher=[[TVNZ]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221212211014/https://www.1news.co.nz/2022/10/16/act-deputy-calls-for-change-to-house-infrastructure-funding/ |archive-date=12 December 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

===2023 general election===
Ahead of the [[2023 New Zealand general election]], van Velden was selected as the ACT party candidate for the eastern Auckland electorate of [[Tāmaki (New Zealand electorate)|Tāmaki]], which had been held by the [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]] since 1960. Van Velden announced she would campaign to win the electorate, instead of campaigning for the party vote only, something the party rarely does outside of their stronghold of [[Epsom (New Zealand electorate)|Epsom]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Trevett |first=Claire | url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/act-partys-brooke-van-velden-targets-national-partys-simon-oconnor-in-bid-for-tamaki-electorate/YFJVVUXNJNDNJKRTQZAPYSXX2I/ | title=Act targets National's Simon O'Connor in bid for Tāmaki seat |date=29 April 2023 |access-date=25 July 2023 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230513143616/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/act-partys-brooke-van-velden-targets-national-partys-simon-oconnor-in-bid-for-tamaki-electorate/YFJVVUXNJNDNJKRTQZAPYSXX2I/ |archive-date=13 May 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> An opinion poll released on 2 October showed van Velden tied with the incumbent, [[Simon O'Connor]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 November 2023|title=Will Act win a second electorate? Poll shows Brooke van Velden closing gap in Tāmaki |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/election-2023-act-partys-brooke-van-velden-hot-on-nats-simon-oconnors-heels-in-tamaki-electorate-poll/W45X53OQOJFCJPZJD62DDBNFEE/ |access-date=1 November 2023 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|language=en-NZ}}</ref> The election night results showed a victory for van Velden, with a majority of 4,158 votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tāmaki – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-49.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231210215708/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-49.html|archive-date=10 December 2023|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=16 October 2023 |title=Out of the blue: Act wins Tamaki electorate |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/first-up/audio/2018911248/out-of-the-blue-act-wins-tamaki-electorate |access-date=27 October 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |language=en-nz}}</ref>

==Second term, 2023–present==
[[File:Brooke van Velden at Emperor's Birthday Celebration Reception February 21, 2025 (cropped).jpg|thumb|267x267px|Van Velden at a celebration of the Japanese Emperor's birthday in 2025]]
Following the formation of the [[Sixth National Government of New Zealand|National-led coalition government]], van Velden became Minister of [[Department of Internal Affairs (New Zealand)|Internal Affairs]] and Minister of Workplace Relations and Safety.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cabinet lineup for new government unveiled - who gets what? |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503156/cabinet-lineup-for-new-government-unveiled-who-gets-what |access-date=15 December 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=24 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204122806/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503156/cabinet-lineup-for-new-government-unveiled-who-gets-what |archive-date=4 December 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Remuneration policies===
As Workplace Relations Minister, she introduced legislation repealing the previous Labour Government's [[Fair Pay Agreements Act 2022]] on 19 December 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fair Pay Agreements Act Repeal Bill |url=https://bills.parliament.nz/v/6/cd76254e-4051-49e6-19e6-08dbfadead1f?Tab=history |publisher=[[New Zealand Parliament]] |access-date=2 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240126103016/https://bills.parliament.nz/v/6/cd76254e-4051-49e6-19e6-08dbfadead1f?Tab=history |archive-date=26 January 2024 |date=19 December 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> Van Velden claimed that fair pay agreements "were never about fairness" but forced "a minority of union worker's views on all affected workers and businesses."<ref>{{cite news |title=Parliament repeals Fair Pay Agreements |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/504707/parliament-repeals-fair-pay-agreements |access-date=2 February 2024 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=14 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240125045502/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/504707/parliament-repeals-fair-pay-agreements |archive-date=25 January 2024}}</ref>

On 1 February 2024, van Velden, as Workplace Relations and Safety Minister, confirmed that the Government would raise the minimum wage by two percent to NZ$23.15 an hour from 1 April 2024.<ref>{{cite news |title=Government announces minimum wage to rise from April 1 |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/02/01/government-announces-minimum-wage-to-rise-from-april-1/ |access-date=5 February 2024 |work=[[1News]] |publisher=[[TVNZ]] |date=1 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240201095834/http://1news.co.nz/2024/02/01/government-announces-minimum-wage-to-rise-from-april-1/ |archive-date=1 February 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> On 2 February Van Velden, as Minister of Internal Affairs, confirmed that the Government would expand the scope of the [[Royal Commission of Inquiry into COVID-19 Lessons Learned]] to include the use of multiple lockdowns, vaccine procurement, the socio-economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on regional and national levels, the cost-effectiveness of the Government's policies, disruptions to public health, education and businesses caused by the Government's policies, and whether the Government response was consistent with the rule of law.<ref>{{cite news |title=Government mulls expanding inquiry into Covid-19 response |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/508262/government-mulls-expanding-inquiry-into-covid-19-response |access-date=2 February 2024 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=2 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240202032025/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/508262/government-mulls-expanding-inquiry-into-covid-19-response |archive-date=2 February 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Holiday Act changes===
In March 2024, van Velden confirmed that the Government was planning to overhaul health and safety regulations and amend the [[Holiday Act 2003]]. She criticised the previous Labour Government's minimum wage increase, designation of [[Matariki]] as a public holiday and doubling of sick leave entitlements for creating business uncertainty and raising the costs of doing business. While [[Business NZ]] welcomed the proposed changes, [[First Union New Zealand]] described the proposed changes as an attack on workers.<ref>{{cite news |title=Major workplace and public holiday changes signalled by Govt |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/03/13/major-workplace-and-public-holiday-changes-signalled-by-govt/ |access-date=15 March 2024 |work=[[1News]] |publisher=[[TVNZ]] |date=13 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240313092107/https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/03/13/major-workplace-and-public-holiday-changes-signalled-by-govt/ |archive-date=13 March 2024}}</ref> ===Equal Pay Amendment Act 2025===
{{Main|Equal Pay Amendment Act 2025}}

On 6 May 2025, van Velden announced that the Government would raise the threshold for making pay equity claims, stating that a 2020 law change had "created problems." As a result, van Velden confirmed that 33 pay equity claims had been stopped. The [[Public Service Association]]'s national secretary Fleur Fitzsimons opposed the changes, claiming that they would make it "impossible for people in female-dominated professions to be paid fairly."<ref>{{cite news |title=Government halts all current pay equity claims, makes it harder to lodge new ones |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/560069/government-halts-all-current-pay-equity-claims-makes-it-harder-to-lodge-new-ones |access-date=7 May 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=6 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250506004237/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/560069/government-halts-all-current-pay-equity-claims-makes-it-harder-to-lodge-new-ones |archive-date=6 May 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> That same day, the Government introduced urgent legislation to raise the pay equity threshold.<ref>{{cite news |title=Pay equity legislation could save 'billions' for government - PM |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/560101/pay-equity-legislation-could-save-billions-for-government-pm |access-date=7 May 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=6 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250507021835/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/560101/pay-equity-legislation-could-save-billions-for-government-pm |archive-date=7 May 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>  The [[Equal Pay Amendment Act 2025]] passed under urgency on 7 May, with the support of the governing coalition parties. Opposition parties opposed the bill.<ref>{{cite news |title=Pay Equity Amendment Bill passes under urgency |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/560257/pay-equity-amendment-bill-passes-under-urgency |access-date=8 May 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=8 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250508060210/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/560257/pay-equity-amendment-bill-passes-under-urgency |archive-date=8 May 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In early May 2025, the [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]]'s leadership apologised after the [[Whangaparāoa]] branch published and deleted a [[Facebook]] post depicting van Velden in a [[Nazi]] military uniform. The post was made in response to the National-led government's legislation raising pay equity thresholds; which van Velden had sponsored. Van Velden described the post as offensive since her grandfather had experienced the [[Netherlands in World War II#German occupation|Nazi occupation of the Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pearse |first1=Adam |title=Local Labour Facebook page reposts - then deletes - image of Brooke van Velden as Nazi |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/labour-party-facebook-page-reposts-then-deletes-image-of-brooke-van-velden-as-nazi/LHUSVVK325DXRDSZCTPXYDK4BE/ |access-date=15 May 2025 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=12 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250515010813/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/deputy-prime-minister-winston-peters-attacks-behaviour-in-parliament-as-degradation/6YZ7F6CF55HFTFMTEVJNA4LLD4/ |archive-date=15 May 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 May, van Velden expressed disagreement during a Parliament debate with [[Stuff (company)|Stuff]] journalist [[Andrea Vance]]'s op-ed newspaper column criticising her and National MPs [[Judith Collins]], [[Erica Stanford]], [[Louise Upston]] and [[Nicola Grigg]] for supporting the Government's pay equity legislation, which Vance argued disproportionately affected predominantly female professions. During the debate, van Velden quoted a passage from Vance's column mentioning the word "[[cunt]]." [[New Zealand First]] leader [[Winston Peters]] criticised van Velden for using what he regarded as inappropriate language while ACT leader Seymour defended van Velden's parliamentary conduct. [[Speaker of the New Zealand House of Representatives|Speaker]] [[Gerry Brownlee]] advised MPs on their use of language in Parliament.<ref>{{cite news |title=Minister drops C-bomb in Parliament while quoting controversial column |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2025/05/14/minister-drops-c-bomb-in-parliament-while-quoting-controversial-column/ |access-date=15 May 2025 |work=[[1News]] |date=14 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250515010721/https://www.1news.co.nz/2025/05/14/minister-drops-c-bomb-in-parliament-while-quoting-controversial-column/ |archive-date=15 May 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Employment Relations Amendment Bill===
{{Main|Employment Relations Amendment Act 2026}} 
On 17 June 2025, van Velden confirmed the Government would be introducing the Employment Relations Amendment Bill into Parliament. Key provisions include changing the distinction between employment and contracting, overhauling the personal grievance process, and allowing employers and employees to negotiate "beneficial terms and conditions." While BusinessNZ director of advocacy Catherine Beard said the proposed legislation would provide more clarity around contract work, the [[Public Service Association]]  national secretary Fleur Fitzsimons and the [[New Zealand Council of Trade Unions]] president Richard Wagstaff expressed concern that the proposed law changes would undermine workers' rights, pay and safety.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pelletier |first1=Nona |title=Employment Relations Act amendments aimed to boost labour market flexibility |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/business/564361/employment-relations-act-amendments-aimed-to-boost-labour-market-flexibility |access-date=18 June 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=17 June 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250618011910/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/business/564361/employment-relations-act-amendments-aimed-to-boost-labour-market-flexibility|archive-date=18 June 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 17 February 2026, the [[Employment Relations Amendment Act 2026]] passed its third reading. It tightened the criteria for personal grievances claims, created a "gateway test" for differentiating between employees and contractors, ended payouts for employees dismissed for "serious misconduct," and eliminated a 30-day rule extending automatic collective agreement terms to new employees. She argued that the new legislation would "maximise business confidence" and accelerate business growth. By contrast, [[E tū]] union national secretary Rachel Mackintosh and Green workplace relations spokesperson [[Teanau Tuiono]] criticised the bill for favouring corporations and employers over workers.<ref>{{cite news |title=Govt's controversial employment relations bill passes third reading |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/02/17/govts-controversial-employment-relations-bill-passes-third-reading/ |access-date=18 February 2026 |work=[[1News]] |date=17 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260218020926/https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/02/17/govts-controversial-employment-relations-bill-passes-third-reading/ |archive-date=18 February 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Road cone tipline===
In early June 2025, the workplace safety agency [[WorkSafe New Zealand]] launched a new [[road cone]] online tipline. As Minister for Workplace Relations and Safety, van Velden said that the new tipline reflected a new shift from "strict enforcement" towards collaboration with businesses and individuals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Govt launches road cone tipline as WorkSafe overhaul begins |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2025/06/03/govt-launches-road-cone-tipline-as-worksafe-overhaul-begins/ |access-date=3 June 2025 |work=[[1News]] |date=3 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603190655/https://www.1news.co.nz/2025/06/03/govt-launches-road-cone-tipline-as-worksafe-overhaul-begins/ |archive-date=3 June 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>  By early June 2025, the hotline had received over 650 reports, with [[Auckland Transport]] receiving nearly 200 reports.<ref>{{cite news |title=How effective has the road cone hotline been? |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/566142/how-effective-has-the-road-cone-hotline-been |access-date=2 February 2026 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=7 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260201005229/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/566142/how-effective-has-the-road-cone-hotline-been |archive-date=1 February 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> By late July 2025, WorkSafe had received 217 reports, with the majority occurring in the [[Auckland Region|Auckland]], [[Wellington Region|Wellington]] and [[Canterbury Region]]s.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Natanahira |first1=Tuwhenuaroa |title=Calls to road cone hot line drop off, latest Worksafe data shows |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/568745/calls-to-road-cone-hot-line-drop-off-latest-worksafe-data-shows |access-date=2 February 2026 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=1 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260201005326/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/568745/calls-to-road-cone-hot-line-drop-off-latest-worksafe-data-shows |archive-date=1 February 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 19 December 2025, the Government shut down the road cone hotline scheme due to deceasing usage and a low volume of valid complaints. The hotline had received about 1,300 notifications over a six-month period and had cost about NZ$150,000. While Labour transport spokesperson [[Tangi Utikere]] described the road cone hotline as a waste of taxpayer money, van Velden argued "that it gave the public a voice, identified the root causes of concern and clarified WorkSafe's role in temporary traffic management."<ref>{{cite news |title=$150,000 road cone hotline an 'absurd' waste of public money - Labour |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/top/585579/150-000-road-cone-hotline-an-absurd-waste-of-public-money-labour |access-date=2 February 2026 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=1 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260202094354/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/top/585579/150-000-road-cone-hotline-an-absurd-waste-of-public-money-labour |archive-date=2 February 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Miscellaneous===
In July 2025, van Velden introduced the Government's proposed online casino legislation, which would introduce 15 licenses for online casinos operating in New Zealand. The bill passed its first reading on 15 July with the support of the ruling coalition and the opposition Green parties.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Palmer |first1=Russell |title=Online casino bill: Greens vote with coalition govt to pass first reading |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/566995/online-casino-bill-greens-vote-with-coalition-govt-to-pass-first-reading |access-date=20 July 2025 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=15 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250716044649/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/566995/online-casino-bill-greens-vote-with-coalition-govt-to-pass-first-reading |archive-date=16 July 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 May van Velden, as [[Minister of Internal Affairs (New Zealand)|Minister of Internal Affairs]], announced that the Government would introduce a [[citizenship test]] focusing on the [[New Zealand Bill of Rights Act 1990|Bill of Rights]], voting rights and government structure for prospective [[New Zealand nationality law|New Zealand citizens]] from mid-2027.<ref>{{cite news |title=New test covering 'responsibilities and privileges' of NZ citizenship announced for migrants |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/594397/new-test-covering-responsibilities-and-privileges-of-nz-citizenship-announced-for-migrants |access-date=7 May 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=6 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260507070754/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/594397/new-test-covering-responsibilities-and-privileges-of-nz-citizenship-announced-for-migrants |archive-date=7 May 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Retirement ===
On 24 March 2026, she announced her retirement from politics and that she wouldn't be running for parliament in the [[2026 New Zealand general election]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-03-24 |title=ACT Party deputy and minister Brooke van Velden retires from politics |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/590461/act-party-deputy-and-minister-brooke-van-velden-retires-from-politics |access-date=2026-03-23 |work=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}}</ref><ref name="z239" /> She was replaced as Deputy Leader of ACT by Nicole McKee on 28 June 2026.<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=28 June 2026 |title=Nicole McKee announced as ACT's new deputy |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/633846/nicole-mckee-announced-as-act-s-new-deputy |access-date=28 June 2026 |website=[[Radio New Zealand]] }}</ref>

== Views and positions ==
Van Velden has stated her reasons for entering politics are to reduce generational debt, improve housing affordability, and provide better mental health for all.<ref name="top contenders">{{cite news |last1=Doyle|first1=Katie |date=1 August 2020|title=Top five contenders who could join ACT leader David Seymour in Parliament |url= https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/422475/top-five-contenders-who-could-join-act-leader-david-seymour-in-parliament |access-date=31 July 2020 |work=[[Radio NZ]]}}</ref> She supported the End of Life Choice Bill based on her belief in freedom of choice.<ref name=":0" /> In a debate about legalising [[Cannabis (drug)|cannabis]], van Velden said that she had smoked it before.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Williams|first=Katarina|date=8 September 2020|title=Cannabis referendum: Election debate sees leaders, minister confess to smoking weed|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/cannabis-referendum/122703050/cannabis-referendum-election-debate-sees-leaders-minister-confess-to-smoking-weed|access-date=22 October 2020|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] }}</ref> She was formerly a [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|Green Party]] voter but switched to supporting ACT while studying economics and international trade at the University of Auckland.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Small |first1=Zane |title=ACT deputy leader Brooke van Velden on why she stopped supporting the Greens |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/10/act-deputy-leader-brooke-van-velden-on-why-she-stopped-supporting-the-greens.html |access-date=23 October 2020 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=22 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023090519/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/10/act-deputy-leader-brooke-van-velden-on-why-she-stopped-supporting-the-greens.html |archive-date=23 October 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2023, she said "When it came to [[COVID-19|COVID]], we completely blew out what the value of a life was, completely, I’ve never seen such a high value on life."<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 November 2023|title=More than a life is worth? |url=https://www.nzdoctor.co.nz/article/opinion/more-life-worth |access-date=2023-12-17 |website=New Zealand Doctor |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Van Velden's parents, Adele<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-14 |title=In pictures: Joy and sadness on Election Night as results roll in |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/500181/in-pictures-joy-and-sadness-on-election-night-as-results-roll-in |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=RNZ |language=en-nz}}</ref> and Robin, were a nurse and mechanic, and later owned car sale firms.<ref>{{Cite news |title= Northern Honda gets new name and owners|url=https://www.pressreader.com/new-zealand/the-northern-advocate6030/20160608/281801398228618 |access-date=2025-03-24 |via=PressReader |date=8 June 2016 |work=Northern Advocate}}</ref> She has three older brothers, Joel, Blake<ref>{{Cite web |title=World Economic Forum |url=https://www.weforum.org/people/blake-van-velden/}}</ref> and Kent.<ref name="Now to Love 2023" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Olive VAN VELDEN Obituary (2024) - Waikato Times |url=https://deaths.waikatotimes.co.nz/nz/obituaries/waikato-times-nz/name/olive-van-velden-obituary?id=54962111 |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref>
